docs.title: CL Forge
docs.text:
Fast, typed Python tools for Chilean data and public APIs.

Get started API reference

CL Forge combines Rust-backed validation utilities with a clean Python interface for the CMF and Mercado Público APIs. It includes synchronous and asynchronous clients, typed responses, configurable HTTP behavior, and flexible credential providers.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
CL Forge supports Python 3.12–3.14.

pip uv 
pip install cl-forge

uv add cl-forge

See the installation guide for source installs and optional dependencies.

docs.title: Validate Chilean identifiers
docs.text:
from cl_forge import Ppu, calculate_verifier, validate_rut

validate_rut(12_345_678, "5")     # True
calculate_verifier(12_345_678)    # "5"

plate = Ppu("PHZF55")
plate.complete                    # "PHZF55-K"
plate.numeric                     # 69455

docs.title: Query CMF indicators
docs.text:
from cl_forge import CmfClient

cmf = CmfClient("your-cmf-api-key")

latest_uf = cmf.uf.latest()
ipc_2025 = cmf.ipc.year(2025)
usd_for_day = cmf.usd.day(2025, 12, 1)

The CMF client provides resources for ipc, uf, utm, usd, eur (also euro), tip, and tmc, plus raw JSON and XML access.

CMF credentials

CMF requests require an API key. You can request one through the CMF API portal.

docs.title: Query Mercado Público
docs.text:
from cl_forge import MarketClient

market = MarketClient("your-mercado-publico-ticket")

active_tenders = market.tender.active()
today_orders = market.order.today()
suppliers = market.supplier.search("70.017.820-K")

The Mercado Público client includes typed resources for tenders, purchase orders, suppliers, and buyers, plus raw v1 and v2 access.

Mercado Público credentials

Mercado Público requests require an API ticket. See the Mercado Público API portal for access details.

docs.title: Use async clients
docs.text:
The asynchronous clients mirror the synchronous resource interface:

from cl_forge import AsyncCmfClient

cmf = AsyncCmfClient("your-cmf-api-key")
latest_uf = await cmf.uf.latest()

docs.title: Credentials and configuration
docs.text:
Pass a credential directly, load it from the environment, or read it from a dotenv file:

export CLFORGE_CMF_API_KEY="your-cmf-api-key"
export CLFORGE_MARKET_API_KEY="your-mercado-publico-ticket"

from cl_forge import ClientConfig, CmfClient, DotEnvCredentials, EnvCredentials

cmf = CmfClient(
    credentials=EnvCredentials(),
    config=ClientConfig(timeout=20, http2=True, retries=5),
)

cmf_from_dotenv = CmfClient(DotEnvCredentials(".env"))

docs.title: Development Setup
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository: 

    git clone https://github.com/matias-scht/cl-forge.git
cd cl-forge

  2. Install dependencies: We use uv for dependency management. 

    uv sync --all-groups

  3. Build the Rust extension: 

    uv run maturin develop

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Create a new branch for your feature or bugfix.
  2. Implement your changes.
  3. Add tests for your changes.
  4. Run tests and linting: 
    uv run pytest
uv run ruff check .
  5. Submit a Pull Request.

docs.title: Code Style
docs.text:
• We use Ruff for Python linting and formatting.
  • Rust code should follow standard cargo fmt guidelines.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: CL Forge is a Python librarie available on PyPI and can be installed using pip, uv or any other Python package manager.

docs.title: From PyPI
docs.text:
uv pip 
uv add cl-forge

pip install cl-forge

docs.title: From Source
docs.text:
Info

Building from source requires a Rust toolchain installed on your system. See Install Rust for more information.

uv pip 
uv add "git+https://github.com/mschiaff/cl-forge.git@<version-tag>"

pip install "git+https://github.com/mschiaff/cl-forge.git@<version-tag>"

Including optional dependencies:

uv pip 
uv add "git+https://github.com/mschiaff/cl-forge.git@<version-tag>[dep1, ...]"

pip install "git+https://github.com/mschiaff/cl-forge.git@<version-tag>[dep1, ...]"

docs.title: Required Dependencies
docs.text:
CL Forge requires the following dependencies:

Package Version pydantic >=2.12.5 httpx2[http2] >=2.12.0 pydantic-settings >=2.14.0

docs.title: Optional Dependencies
docs.text:
CL Forge has several optional dependencies, although none are actually required to support any functionality. They are more of a convenience to support likely uses.

Analytics Recommendations

If you are planning on using CL Forge to get, manipulate and export data from API clients, we strongly recommend installing the analytics tag. If you're working on a Jupyter Notebook environment, we encourage you to also include the notebook tag.

Using uv: 

uv add "cl-forge[analytics, notebook]"

Or using pip: 

pip install "cl-forge[analytics, notebook]"

Why?

Polars is a fast and memory efficient dataframe library that stands out for its performance. Furthermore, parsing lists of Pydantic models into polars dataframes is quite straightforward:

import polars as pl

data: list[BaseModel] = ...
df = pl.DataFrame(data)

docs.text: Tag Description polars Convert data to and from polars dataframes/series pandas Convert data to and from pandas dataframes/series pyarrow Convert data to and from pyarrow tables/arrays interop Installs all interoperability dependencies

docs.text: Tag Description calamine Read from Excel files using the calamine engine openpyxl Read from Excel files using the openpyxl engine xlsxwriter Write to Excel files using the xlsxwriter engine excel Installs all Excel dependencies

docs.title: Others
docs.text: Tag Description notebook Installs Jupyter Notebook support dependencies analytics Installs data analytics suggested dependencies all Installs all optional dependencies but the ones from development

docs.title: Dependency Groups
docs.text:
Info

These aren't extras you can install, but rather dependency groups defined in the uv configuration for development purposes.

Example 
git clone https://github.com/mschiaff/cl-forge.git
cd cl-forge
uv sync --group build

docs.title: cl_forge.Ppu
docs.text:
Ppu(ppu: str)

Represents a Chilean PPU (vehicle license plate).

Attributes:

Name Type Description raw str

The input PPU.

numeric int

The numeric representation of the PPU.

normalized str

The normalized PPU.

verifier str

The calculated verifier digit of the PPU.

format str

The detected format of the PPU. Supported formats:

  • LLLNN -> 3 letters followed by 2 digits
  • LLLNNN -> 4 letters followed by 3 digits
  • LLLLNN -> 4 letters followed by 2 digits
  • LLNNNN -> 2 letters followed by 4 digits
complete str

The normalized PPU with the verifier digit, separated by '-'.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default ppu str

Chilean PPU (vehicle license plate).

required

docs.title: cl_forge.calculate_verifier
docs.text:
calculate_verifier(digits: int) -> str

Calculates the verifier digit (DV) of a Chilean RUT/RUN using Module 11 algorithm.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default digits int

Numeric part of the RUT/RUN (digits only).

required

Returns:

Type Description str

Verifier digit: '0'..'9' or 'K'.

docs.title: cl_forge.validate_rut
docs.text:
validate_rut(digits: int, verifier: str) -> bool

Validates a Chilean RUT/RUN by checking if the provided verifier digit matches the calculated one using Module 11 algorithm.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default digits int

Numeric part of the RUT/RUN (digits only).

required verifier str

Verifier digit to validate against: "0".."9" or "K".

required

Returns:

Type Description bool

True if the verifier is valid for the given correlative, False otherwise.
